# Depth and Geometry Supervision

Also called: Depth-supervised NeRF, Geometric regularization, Depth priors in NeRF

## Overview
Depth and Geometry Supervision methods accelerate [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) optimization and improve geometric accuracy by incorporating external depth estimates or structural constraints into the training loss. Unlike standard [photometric optimization](#5790-photometric-optimization.md), which suffers from shape-radiance ambiguity and slow convergence in textureless regions, these methods constrain the density field $\sigma$ to align with known geometric surfaces [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]. This family is distinguished from sibling methods like [Diffusion-Regularized NeRF Training](7381-diffusion-regularized-nerf-training.md) by relying on explicit depth values or structural consistency rather than learned generative priors, and from [Geometric Baseline Regularization](7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md) by focusing on alignment with specific depth targets rather than general smoothness or sparsity.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the fundamental structure of an augmented loss function. The [total loss](#4177-total-loss-function.md) $\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}}$ is a weighted sum of the standard photometric reconstruction loss and one or more [regularization terms](#1413-regularization-losses.md) $\mathcal{L}_k$:

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{photo}} + \sum_k \lambda_k \mathcal{L}_k $$

where $\lambda_k$ are hyperparameters controlling the strength of each regularizer [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]. The photometric loss is typically the [Mean Squared Error](#1651-mse-loss-and-psnr-conversion.md) (MSE) between the rendered color $\mathbf{C}$ and the ground truth image $I$:

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\text{photo}} = || \mathbf{C} - I ||_2^2 $$

Regularization terms $\mathcal{L}_k$ operate on the density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ fields or the rendered weights $w_i$ to constrain the solution space [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]. Common strategies include enforcing spatial smoothness, ensuring geometric consistency across views, or aligning the output distribution with learned priors.

## Subtopics

### [Guided Optimization of NeRF](7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md)
[Guided Optimization of NeRF](#7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md) mitigates the shape-radiance ambiguity inherent in [Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) ([NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)) for indoor scenes by restricting the sampling of points along camera rays to ranges derived from adapted monocular [depth priors](#7616-depth-regularization.md). Unlike [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md), which samples uniformly between sparse reconstruction bounds, this method uses multi-view consistency checks to define adaptive near and far bounds, ensuring sampled points concentrate around plausible geometry. It further refines the output depth map using confidence scores derived from RGB reconstruction errors and plane bilateral filtering.

### [Single-view NeRF Training with Depth Map](8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md)
This method addresses the under-constrained optimization problem of reconstructing a 3D scene from a single panoramic input by initializing the NeRF geometry using estimated depth maps. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Depth-Supervised NeRF](8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md) by explicitly performing a deformable alignment of multiple perspective depth estimates into a canonical panorama before training, rather than applying [depth loss](#7487-pseudo-depth-supervised-loss.md) directly to raw estimates or using multi-view consistency. It builds on [Depth and Geometry Supervision](8727-depth-and-geometry-supervision.md) by providing a robust initialization strategy for visible regions.

### [Depth-Supervised NeRF](8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md)
Depth-Supervised NeRF (DS-NeRF) is a training procedure that accelerates Neural [Radiance Field optimization](#44-radiance-field-optimization.md) and improves quality with sparse input views by incorporating depth supervision from sparse 3D keypoints generated during Structure-from-Motion (SfM) preprocessing. Unlike methods that rely on data-driven priors from category-specific training data (e.g., [pixelNeRF](#7471-pixelnerf.md), metaNeRF) or semantic consistency, DS-NeRF only requires the existence of 3D keypoints, making it flexible and not dependent on training data distribution assumptions. It enforces that the ray termination distribution matches [surface priors](#9270-geometry-and-surface-priors.md), reducing overfitting and speeding up training by 2-3x.

### [Depth Structural Consistency Regularization](9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md)
[Depth Structural Consistency Regularization](#9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md) (RDSC) is a geometric regularization term used in NeRF training to enforce continuity constraints on rendered depth maps based on priors from external depth estimation models (e.g., DepthAnythingV2). It differs from standard depth supervision by explicitly penalizing structural discontinuities between neighboring pixels in the rendered depth field that contradict the smoothness or boundary structure observed in the reference depth map, rather than just minimizing point-wise depth errors. It builds on [Depth and Geometry Supervision](8727-depth-and-geometry-supervision.md).

### Zero-level set projection
- **Definition:** Refines inaccurate median depth from a pre-trained NeRF, particularly at grazing view angles, by iteratively projecting points onto the zero level-set of the surface using TSDF values [S1].
- **Step:** For each 3D point $p$ on the viewing ray, perform exactly 4 iterative gradient descent steps along the ray direction using the TSDF predicted value to update the point position [S1].
- **Formula:** $p_{new} = p_{old} + \alpha \times \hat{t}$, where $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}] = \phi(p)$; $p$ is the current 3D point, $\alpha$ is a small constant step size, $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}]$ are the tangent, normal, and feature outputs from network $\phi$ evaluated at $p$ [S1].
- **Parameter:** $\alpha$: Small constant controlling the step size of the gradient descent update. Value not specified in this section [S1].
- **Pitfall:** Median depth from a pre-trained NeRF becomes inaccurate when the angle between the view direction and the surface is small (grazing angles) [S1].
- **Usage:** Applied in NeRFMeshing as a preprocessing step to initialize the mesh geometry before training the SSAN model [S1].

### Robust Depth Loss
- **Definition:** A loss function designed to address geometry error degradation in extrapolation performance by being less sensitive to outliers than [L2 loss](#6038-mean-square-error-mse.md), encouraging NeRF to terminate rays around pseudo depth while retaining freedom for inaccurate geometry [S2].
- **Formula:** $\mathcal {L}_{\text {robust}}(\mathbf {r}) = \begin {cases} 0.5\Delta {D}(\mathbf {r})^{2}, &\text {if } \Delta {D}(\mathbf {r}) < \beta \\ \beta ^ {2} (0.5 + \log (\frac {\Delta {D}(\mathbf {r})}{\beta })), &\text {otherwise } \end {cases}$ where $\Delta D(\mathbf{r}) = \hat{D}(\mathbf{r}) - D(\mathbf{r})$ is the absolute depth difference, $\beta$ is a constant set to 0.1, and $\hat{D}(\mathbf{r})$ is the depth expectation along the camera axis of ray $r(t)$ [S2].
- **Parameter:** $\beta$: A constant threshold for the robust depth loss, set to 0.1 throughout the experiments [S2].

### Statistical Depth Refinement
- **Definition:** A post-processing step during training to handle corrupt stereo depth caused by fuzzy pixels and specular highlights, preventing overfitting to corrupt depth which leads to abrupt artifacts [S3].
- **Step:** Obtain the underfitting output depth maps $D_b^K_i$ for the $i$-th frame after $K$ iterations of training. Compute residual maps between the underfitting depth and the stereo depth: $i = |D_b^K_i - D_i|$. Compute a probabilistic distribution over the residual maps. Set a threshold parameter $\alpha \in [0, 1]$ and locate pixels with the last $\alpha$-quantile residuals (largest residuals). Identify these located pixels as corrupt depth and replace them with the smoother depth values from the underfitting output $D_b^K_i$. Optimize the radiance fields on the patched depth maps in subsequent training iterations [S3].
- **Parameter:** The depth refinement [iteration count](#1244-iteration-based-coloring.md) $K$ is set to 4000 [S3].

### Depth Supervision with Planar Architectural Depth Priors
- **Definition:** Incorporates precomputed depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls into NeRF training to enforce geometric constraints on textureless planar surfaces [S4].
- **Step:** 1. Compute depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls using semantic segmentation. 2. Incorporate these priors into training with MSE and BoundL losses alongside photometric loss. 3. Train until convergence [S4].
- **Parameter:** $\delta$ (BoundL tolerance): 1 mm. $\lambda_{color}$: 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room). $\lambda_{depth}$: 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room) [S4].
- **Number:** RMSE of priors vs ground truth: 2.786 mm (bedroom), 3.201 mm (living room). Converged in 120,000 iterations [S4].
- **Comparison:** Faster convergence than photometric-only (120k vs 200k) and patch-regularization (120k vs 280k) methods due to depth supervision enabling quick identification of empty spaces, concentrating sampling on occupied regions, and providing a stronger optimization signal [S4].

## Background
The integration of depth supervision into NeRF training originated from the need to resolve the shape-radiance ambiguity, where multiple geometry configurations can produce the same photometric output, particularly in textureless regions [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Early approaches like Depth-Supervised NeRF (DS-NeRF) utilized sparse 3D keypoints from Structure-from-Motion (SfM) to guide ray termination distributions, significantly accelerating convergence compared to photometric-only training [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Subsequent works expanded this to include dense depth priors from monocular estimators, requiring techniques like deformable alignment for single-view scenarios [8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md] or structural consistency regularization to handle noise in external depth maps [9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md]. Methods such as NeRFMeshing introduced geometric post-processing steps like zero-level set projection to refine mesh extraction from [implicit fields](#1800-implicit-surface-primitives.md) [S1]. More recent variants have explored robust loss functions to handle inaccurate pseudo-depths [S2] and statistical refinement to filter corrupt stereo depth in specific domains like robotic surgery [S3].
